ottopreminger.description: A Viennese stage director turned Hollywood producer-director. His films present institutions and trials from all sides without telling the viewer what to think.

facts.text: Challenged Hollywood's Production Code with The Moon Is Blue and The Man with the Golden Arm.
Credited the blacklisted writer Dalton Trumbo on Exodus.

robertaldrich.signature: Made brutal, cynical genre films shot from skewed angles.
robertaldrich.description: An independent-minded director of war films, westerns and thrillers whose heroes are often as ugly as their enemies.

facts.text: Kiss Me Deadly ends with a nuclear glow escaping from a mysterious box.
Was an assistant director to Renoir and Chaplin.

tobehooper.signature: Made one of the most frightening films ever on a shoestring in the Texas heat.
tobehooper.description: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre feels like found evidence: grainy 16mm, relentless noise and almost no relief.

facts.text: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre shows far less blood than its reputation suggests.
Directed Poltergeist, produced by Steven Spielberg.

robertjflaherty.signature: Often called the father of the documentary, though he staged much of what he filmed.
robertjflaherty.description: An explorer who lived with his subjects for long periods and filmed their struggle with nature as romantic drama.

facts.text: Nanook of the North was shot in the Canadian Arctic; several scenes were re-enacted for the camera.
Co-directed Tabu with F. W. Murnau.

alfonsocuaron.signature: Known for immersive long takes that follow characters through chaos.
alfonsocuaron.description: A Mexican director who moves between Hollywood spectacle and personal films. His camera roams continuously, taking in the background as much as the leads.

facts.text: Has worked with the cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki since film school.
Shot Roma himself, in black and white.
Won Best Director Oscars for Gravity and Roma.

luisgarciaberlanga.signature: Smuggled savage satire past Franco's censors in crowded long takes.
luisgarciaberlanga.description: His comedies fill the frame with people talking at once while the camera weaves between them. Under the jokes they are bleak portraits of Spanish society.

facts.text: Wrote his best-known films with Rafael Azcona.
El Verdugo is a comedy about a reluctant executioner.

mikhailkalatozov.signature: Sent the camera flying through crowds, up stairwells and across rooftops.
mikhailkalatozov.description: A Georgian-born director whose films with the cinematographer Sergei Urusevsky are among the most acrobatic ever shot.

facts.text: I Am Cuba was forgotten for decades until its revival in the 1990s.

gusvansant.signature: Alternates between studio films and minimalist experiments that follow young people on foot.
gusvansant.description: Based in Portland, Oregon. His most personal films trail drifters and teenagers in long walking shots and refuse to explain them.

facts.text: Has said Béla Tarr's long takes inspired his Death trilogy.

frederickwiseman.signature: Has documented institutions for almost sixty years without narration or interviews.
frederickwiseman.description: Each film observes one institution, a hospital, a school, a welfare office, and finds its structure in the editing.

facts.text: Titicut Follies was restricted from public screening in Massachusetts for over two decades.
Trained as a lawyer.
Edits his own films, often to three hours or more.

andywarhol.signature: Turned on the camera and let time and his superstars do the rest.
andywarhol.description: The pop artist made hundreds of films at his Factory in the 1960s, many of them single unedited reels of people sleeping, eating or talking.

facts.text: Empire is an eight-hour static shot of the Empire State Building.
Chelsea Girls was projected on two screens side by side.

manoeldeoliveira.signature: Made films from the silent era until he was over a hundred.
manoeldeoliveira.description: The Portuguese director's late films are stately, literary and theatrical, filmed in fixed shots where actors speak the text out toward the audience.

facts.text: Directed his first film in 1931 and his last in his 106th year.
Made most of his films after the age of seventy.

terencedavies.signature: Turned his Liverpool childhood into slow tracking shots and communal singing.
terencedavies.description: His autobiographical films are organised by memory instead of plot: songs, radio voices and tableaux of family life that dissolve into each other.

facts.text: Distant Voices, Still Lives is structured around family songs and photographs.
Later made films about Emily Dickinson and Siegfried Sassoon.

peterbogdanovich.signature: A critic who became a director to keep classical Hollywood alive.
peterbogdanovich.description: He interviewed the old masters before directing films in their manner, in deep-focus black and white or as screwball comedy.

facts.text: Shot The Last Picture Show in black and white on Orson Welles's advice.
Published book-length interviews with Ford, Hawks and Welles.

mayaderen.signature: Founded the American avant-garde film with a fourteen-minute dream.
mayaderen.description: A dancer, theorist and organiser as well as a filmmaker. Her films cut between places on a single movement and loop events like a recurring dream.

facts.text: Made Meshes of the Afternoon with her husband Alexander Hammid at their Los Angeles home.
Distributed and lectured on her own films, creating a model for independent cinema.

georgemiller.signature: Stages vehicular action as pure visual storytelling.
georgemiller.description: An Australian doctor turned director. The Mad Max films are chases told almost without dialogue, cut fast but composed so the eye never loses its place.

facts.text: Worked as a doctor while making the first Mad Max.
Also directed Babe: Pig in the City and Happy Feet.
Mad Max: Fury Road keeps the point of interest in the centre of the frame so that fast cuts stay readable.

pedrocosta.signature: Films Lisbon's poorest immigrants as if painting by candlelight.
pedrocosta.description: Since the late 1990s he has worked with the residents of a demolished Lisbon slum, filming their stories in long, dark, carefully lit fixed shots.

facts.text: Shot In Vanda's Room almost alone with a small digital camera over many months.
Works repeatedly with people from the Fontainhas district.

henrigeorgesclouzot.signature: France's master of suspense and misanthropy.
henrigeorgesclouzot.description: His thrillers are meticulously planned and pitiless about human motives. Le Corbeau, made during the occupation, got him banned from filmmaking for a time after the liberation.

facts.text: Bought the rights to the novel behind Diabolique before Hitchcock could.
The Wages of Fear also won the Golden Bear in Berlin.

aleksandrsokurov.signature: Tarkovsky's protégé, who bends and tints the image like an old painting.
aleksandrsokurov.description: A Russian director of elegies and portraits of power. He distorts the picture with lenses and filters until it resembles tarnished paint.

facts.text: Russian Ark is a single unbroken 96-minute shot through the Hermitage.
Won the Golden Lion for Faust.

ritwikghatak.signature: Made the Partition of Bengal the wound at the centre of all his films.
ritwikghatak.description: A Bengali contemporary of Satyajit Ray with the opposite temperament: operatic, jagged and angry, using melodrama and startling sound.

facts.text: Taught at the Film and Television Institute of India, where he shaped a generation of directors.
Completed only eight features.

samuelfuller.signature: A tabloid reporter and infantryman who made films like front-page headlines.
samuelfuller.description: He wrote, produced and directed low-budget war films, westerns and crime stories that hit taboo subjects head on.

facts.text: Fought in the Second World War and filmed the liberation of a concentration camp.
Appears in Godard's Pierrot le Fou, declaring that film is like a battleground.

paulverhoeven.signature: A Dutch provocateur who hid satire inside violent Hollywood blockbusters.
paulverhoeven.description: After a controversial career in the Netherlands he made American science fiction and thrillers that push sex and violence until they become commentary.

facts.text: Holds a doctorate in mathematics and physics.
Collected his Golden Raspberry award for Showgirls in person.
RoboCop and Starship Troopers include mock commercials and newsreels.

emirkusturica.signature: Fills the frame with brass bands, animals and chaos.
emirkusturica.description: A Sarajevo-born director whose films treat Yugoslav history as a carnival, somewhere between Fellini and a wedding party out of control.

facts.text: Plays in the band The No Smoking Orchestra.

louismalle.signature: The New Wave's restless outsider, who never made the same kind of film twice.
louismalle.description: He moved between thrillers, documentaries, scandal and autobiography, and between France and the United States.

facts.text: Miles Davis improvised the score of Elevator to the Gallows.
Co-directed The Silent World with Jacques Cousteau.
My Dinner with Andre is a single dinner conversation.

johnboorman.signature: Drawn to myth, quests and men tested by the wilderness.
johnboorman.description: A British director who has worked on both sides of the Atlantic. His films push genre stories toward legend.

facts.text: Point Blank brought European fragmentation to the American crime film.
Hope and Glory is based on his childhood in the London Blitz.

robertwise.signature: A former editor who worked expertly in every genre.
robertwise.description: He directed horror, noir, science fiction and two of the most successful musicals ever made, adapting his style to each.

facts.text: Edited Citizen Kane.
Won Best Director Oscars for West Side Story and The Sound of Music.

arthurpenn.signature: Opened the door to New Hollywood with the gunfire that ends Bonnie and Clyde.
arthurpenn.description: Came from live television and Broadway. He brought French New Wave abruptness to American genres.

facts.text: Bonnie and Clyde was first offered to Truffaut and Godard.
Its ending was filmed with several cameras running at different speeds.

alexandermackendrick.signature: Made Ealing's darkest comedies, then Hollywood's most acid film about power.
alexandermackendrick.description: A Scottish-American director whose comedies have a streak of cruelty unusual for Ealing Studios.

facts.text: Directed The Ladykillers and The Man in the White Suit at Ealing.
Left directing to teach at CalArts.

victorsjostrom.signature: The father of Swedish cinema, who made nature an actor.
victorsjostrom.description: His silent films use real landscapes and weather as moral forces, a decade before this was common.

facts.text: The Phantom Carriage used multiple exposures for its ghosts.
Played the old professor in Bergman's Wild Strawberries.

leoscarax.signature: The romantic wild child of French cinema.
leoscarax.description: He appeared in the 1980s as a prodigy steeped in silent film and Godard. His few films are extravagant, lovesick and full of sudden bursts of movement.

facts.text: Denis Lavant has starred in most of his films.
Les Amants du Pont-Neuf required a replica of the Paris bridge to be built in the south of France.

georgestevens.signature: Moved from light comedy to monumental American dramas after the war.
georgestevens.description: A former cameraman who shot Laurel and Hardy. After the war his films became slower, graver and more deliberate.

facts.text: Filmed the liberation of Dachau as head of a US Army film unit.
Used slow dissolves as a signature in A Place in the Sun.

margueriteduras.signature: A novelist who separated voices from images.
margueriteduras.description: One of France's major writers, she directed films in which what we hear and what we see drift apart.

facts.text: Wrote the screenplay of Hiroshima mon amour.
In India Song the dialogue is heard entirely off screen and never lip-synced.

cooperschoedsack.signature: Two adventurer-documentarists who invented the monster movie.
cooperschoedsack.description: They filmed expeditions in Persia and Siam before turning their own exploits into the story of a film crew that brings back a giant ape.

facts.text: Made the expedition documentaries Grass and Chang before King Kong.
Kong was animated frame by frame by Willis O'Brien.
They appear as the airmen who shoot Kong down.

ermannoolmi.signature: Carried neorealism on quietly for decades, with real workers and peasants.
ermannoolmi.description: Started by making documentaries for an electricity company. His features observe work and ritual with patience and gentle humour.

facts.text: He shot and edited it himself, with Lombard farmers speaking their own dialect.

wachowskis.signature: Fused Hong Kong action, anime and philosophy into The Matrix.
wachowskis.description: Sisters who write and direct together. Their films are maximalist, sincere and built from many sources at once.

facts.text: The bullet-time effect used a ring of still cameras.
Hired the Hong Kong choreographer Yuen Woo-ping to train the cast.

gwpabst.description: Associated with the New Objectivity that followed Expressionism. He was praised for psychological realism and for editing so smooth that cuts pass unnoticed.

facts.text: Cast the American actress Louise Brooks as Lulu in Pandora's Box.
Known for cutting on movement to hide his edits.

feimu.signature: Made what is often voted the greatest Chinese film.
feimu.description: A Shanghai director of the 1930s and 1940s. Spring in a Small Town is a restrained triangle among ruins, narrated by the wife.

facts.text: Spring in a Small Town was dismissed after 1949 and rediscovered in the 1980s.
Tian Zhuangzhuang remade it in 2002.

josephlosey.signature: A blacklisted American who dissected the English class system.
josephlosey.description: After leaving Hollywood he rebuilt his career in Britain, where his films turn houses into arenas of class and sexual power.

facts.text: Made three films with the playwright Harold Pinter, including The Servant.
Left the United States in the early 1950s during the blacklist.

lynneramsay.signature: Tells stories through texture, sound and fragments instead of dialogue.
lynneramsay.description: A Glasgow-born director who trained as a photographer. Her films stay inside damaged characters and show us details in place of explanations.

facts.text: Trained as a photographer.
Works slowly: years pass between her films.

jonathandemme.signature: A humanist with a habit of having actors look straight into the lens.
jonathandemme.description: Started with Roger Corman and moved between comedies, thrillers, documentaries and concert films with the same generosity toward his characters.

facts.text: The Silence of the Lambs won the five major Oscars.
Stop Making Sense is often called the best concert film.

jameswhale.signature: Gave Universal's monsters wit, pathos and Expressionist shadows.
jameswhale.description: An English stage director who made four classic horror films in the early 1930s, each laced with sly humour.

facts.text: Came from the London stage.
Bride of Frankenstein mixes horror with camp comedy.

barryjenkins.signature: Films Black intimacy in saturated colour, with faces looking straight at us.
barryjenkins.description: His films are tender, music-led studies of love and identity, shaped by Asian and European art cinema as much as by American tradition.

facts.text: Moonlight is told in three chapters, with three actors playing the same character.
Has cited Wong Kar-wai and Claire Denis as influences.

todbrowning.signature: A former circus performer drawn to sideshows and outcasts.
todbrowning.description: His silent melodramas with Lon Chaney and his early sound films return again and again to the carnival and to bodies that society rejects.

facts.text: Freaks cast real sideshow performers and was banned in Britain for decades.
Made ten films with Lon Chaney.
Directed Bela Lugosi in Dracula.

peterjackson.signature: Went from splatter comedies to filming The Lord of the Rings in his native New Zealand.
peterjackson.description: A self-taught filmmaker who built an effects industry in Wellington to realise his projects.

facts.text: Shot all three Lord of the Rings films back to back.
The Return of the King won all eleven Oscars it was nominated for.

timburton.signature: Makes gothic fairy tales about gentle misfits.
timburton.description: A former Disney animator whose design-led films draw on German Expressionism, 1950s monster movies and suburbia.

facts.text: Began as an animator at Disney.
Has worked with the composer Danny Elfman on nearly all his films.

jonasmekas.signature: The godfather of American avant-garde cinema and its tireless diarist.
jonasmekas.description: A Lithuanian refugee who arrived in New York in 1949. He filmed his daily life in brief bursts for seven decades and edited the footage into long diary films.

facts.text: Co-founded Anthology Film Archives and the Film-Makers' Cooperative.
Wrote a film column for The Village Voice.

larisashepitko.signature: Made stark moral dramas before dying at 41.
larisashepitko.description: A Ukrainian-born director whose films test individual conscience in extreme conditions, shot in harsh black and white.

facts.text: The Ascent won the Golden Bear in 1977.
Studied under Alexander Dovzhenko.
Died in a car accident in 1979 while preparing her next film.

darioargento.signature: The maestro of the Italian giallo, with murders staged like opera in primary colours.
darioargento.description: His thrillers and supernatural horror films care less about logic than about colour, architecture, music and the killer's point of view.

facts.text: Suspiria was printed with an old Technicolor process for its saturated colour.
Co-wrote the story of Once Upon a Time in the West.
Often works with the band Goblin.

sofiacoppola.signature: Films privileged boredom and loneliness from the inside.
sofiacoppola.description: Her films are mood pieces about young women in gilded isolation, built on atmosphere and music more than plot.

facts.text: Won the screenplay Oscar for Lost in Translation.
Is the daughter of Francis Ford Coppola.
Won Best Director at Cannes for The Beguiled.

johnschlesinger.signature: Moved from the British New Wave to a jagged portrait of New York.
johnschlesinger.description: Began in BBC documentaries. His 1960s films follow restless young people in a changing Britain.

facts.text: Midnight Cowboy is the only X-rated film to win Best Picture.
Began in BBC documentaries.

gurudutt.signature: The melancholy poet of Hindi cinema's golden age.
gurudutt.description: Actor, producer and director. His films use song sequences, sweeping crane shots and deep shadows to tell stories of artists rejected by the world.

facts.text: Starred in his own films.
Kaagaz Ke Phool was the first Indian film in CinemaScope and a commercial failure.
Worked with the cinematographer V. K. Murthy.

michelgondry.signature: A music-video inventor who prefers handmade, in-camera tricks.
michelgondry.description: A French director who brought the playful illusions of his videos into features about memory and dreams.

facts.text: Made videos for Björk, Daft Punk and The White Stripes.
Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind was written by Charlie Kaufman.

frankborzage.signature: Hollywood's great romantic, for whom love overcomes poverty and war.
frankborzage.description: His couples are poor, threatened and transfigured by devotion, filmed in soft light on stylised studio sets.

facts.text: Won the first Best Director Oscar for a dramatic picture, for 7th Heaven.
Made a series of films pairing Janet Gaynor and Charles Farrell.

alanjpakula.description: His thrillers dwarf their characters in dark, wide, architectural frames, suggesting forces they cannot see.

facts.text: Klute, The Parallax View and All the President's Men are known as his paranoia trilogy.
Shot all three with the cinematographer Gordon Willis.

tomasgutierrezalea.signature: Cuba's leading filmmaker, loyal to the revolution and critical of it.
tomasgutierrezalea.description: His films examine life after the revolution with irony, mixing fiction with documentary material.

facts.text: Co-founded the Cuban film institute ICAIC.
Memories of Underdevelopment mixes fiction with newsreel and photographs.

kinghu.signature: Turned the martial arts film into visual poetry.
kinghu.description: Working in Hong Kong and Taiwan, he drew on Peking opera for the rhythm of his fight scenes and on landscape painting for his compositions.

facts.text: A Touch of Zen won a technical prize at Cannes in 1975.
Its bamboo forest duel is echoed in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.

anthonymann.signature: Made westerns in which the landscape mirrors tormented heroes.
anthonymann.description: He moved from shadowy low-budget noirs to psychologically harsh westerns and then to epics.

facts.text: Made five westerns with James Stewart.
Shot his 1940s noirs with the cinematographer John Alton.

royandersson.signature: Builds each scene as one fixed, pale tableau of human absurdity.
royandersson.description: A Swedish director whose late films are chains of vignettes, each a single deep-focus shot on a hand-built set with chalk-faced actors.

facts.text: Builds his sets in his own Stockholm studio.
Financed his features by directing hundreds of commercials.
Won the Golden Lion for A Pigeon Sat on a Branch Reflecting on Existence.

kathrynbigelow.signature: Makes action films about addiction to danger.
kathrynbigelow.description: Trained as a painter. Her films put the viewer inside physical risk with restless, subjective camerawork.

facts.text: Was the first woman to win the Best Director Oscar, for The Hurt Locker.
Trained as a painter.

georgesfranju.signature: Found poetry in horror and horror in the everyday.
georgesfranju.description: He moved from unsettling documentaries to dreamlike thrillers that pay homage to silent serials.

facts.text: Co-founded the Cinémathèque française with Henri Langlois.
Blood of the Beasts documents the slaughterhouses of Paris.

jacquesbecker.signature: A craftsman of gestures, friendship and work.
jacquesbecker.description: His films attend to how people do things: cook, dress, dig a tunnel. The New Wave critics admired him as a model of precise, unpretentious craft.

facts.text: Was Jean Renoir's assistant through the 1930s.
Le Trou cast a man who had taken part in the real prison escape it depicts.

louisfeuillade.signature: The king of the crime serial.
louisfeuillade.description: As head of production at Gaumont he made hundreds of films. His serials stage wild plots in real Paris streets, in calm deep-focus long shots.

facts.text: The Surrealists adored Fantômas and Les Vampires.
Olivier Assayas's Irma Vep is about a remake of Les Vampires.

hongsangsoo.signature: Makes film after film about awkward drinking sessions, with a sudden zoom as his signature.
hongsangsoo.description: A prolific South Korean director of small, playful films in which stories repeat with variations.

facts.text: Often writes each day's scenes on the morning of the shoot.
Releases one or two features a year.

lindsayanderson.signature: The angriest voice of the British New Wave.
lindsayanderson.description: A critic and documentarist before his first feature. His films attack British institutions with a mix of realism and Brechtian fantasy.

facts.text: Founded the Free Cinema documentary movement.
If.... switches between colour and black and white.

errolmorris.signature: Has his subjects look straight into the lens and re-enacts their stories in stylised detail.
errolmorris.description: His documentaries are investigations into self-deception, combining interviews with re-enactments and a driving score.

facts.text: The Thin Blue Line helped free a man wrongly convicted of murder.
Invented the Interrotron so that interviewees meet the viewer's eye.
Worked as a private detective.

juliedash.signature: Told Black women's history in a lyrical, non-linear style.
juliedash.description: A member of the L.A. Rebellion. Daughters of the Dust portrays a Gullah family in 1902 through ritual, memory and landscape.

facts.text: Daughters of the Dust was the first feature by an African American woman to get a general theatrical release in the United States.
Its imagery was a reference for Beyoncé's Lemonade.

francescorosi.signature: Invented the film investigation into power, crime and the Italian state.
francescorosi.description: His films reconstruct real cases as open inquiries, leaving the questions unanswered because the facts are.

facts.text: Was Visconti's assistant on La Terra Trema.
Salvatore Giuliano hardly shows the bandit it is named after.
Hands over the City won the Golden Lion.

fredzinnemann.description: A Viennese émigré trained in documentary. His films place one person's principles against a community's cowardice.

facts.text: High Noon unfolds in close to real time.
Worked on People on Sunday in Berlin alongside Robert Siodmak, Edgar Ulmer and Billy Wilder.
Won Best Director Oscars for From Here to Eternity and A Man for All Seasons.

reneclair.signature: Brought the lightness of silent comedy into the sound era.
reneclair.description: He came out of the Paris avant-garde and made some of the first inventive sound films, treating music and noise as comedy.

facts.text: His Dada short Entr'acte featured Man Ray and Marcel Duchamp.
The producers of À nous la liberté accused Chaplin's Modern Times of borrowing from it.

raulruiz.signature: A Chilean exile who made over a hundred labyrinthine films.
raulruiz.description: His stories branch, loop and contradict themselves, with a playful love of puzzles, ghosts and tall tales.

facts.text: Left Chile after the 1973 coup and worked mainly in France.
Adapted Proust in Time Regained.

giuseppetornatore.description: A Sicilian director of sweeping, sentimental films about memory and the pull of home.

facts.text: Cinema Paradiso won the foreign-language Oscar.
Worked repeatedly with the composer Ennio Morricone.

jeanrouch.signature: An anthropologist who invented cinéma vérité and inspired the New Wave.
jeanrouch.description: He made most of his films in West Africa, improvising stories together with the people he filmed.

facts.text: Chronicle of a Summer ends with its participants discussing the film they have just watched.
Often asked his subjects to improvise the commentary over the footage afterwards.

sydneypollack.signature: A reliable maker of star-driven Hollywood dramas and comedies.
sydneypollack.description: A former actor and acting teacher, valued by stars for the performances he drew from them.

facts.text: Made seven films with Robert Redford.
Won the Best Director Oscar for Out of Africa.
Also acted, including in his own Tootsie.

borisbarnet.signature: The lightest touch in Soviet cinema.
borisbarnet.description: A pupil of Lev Kuleshov who preferred comedy, feeling and everyday detail to political argument.

facts.text: Was a boxer before joining Lev Kuleshov's workshop.
Outskirts was an early Soviet sound film.

johnwaters.description: He made deliberately shocking underground comedies with a troupe of friends and later brought the same sensibility to the mainstream.

facts.text: Cast the drag performer Divine in his early films.
Hairspray became a Broadway musical.

roberthamer.signature: Made the most elegant and poisonous of the Ealing comedies.
roberthamer.description: A former editor. Kind Hearts and Coronets tells of serial murder in the politest possible voice-over.

facts.text: In Kind Hearts and Coronets Alec Guinness plays eight members of one family.
Directed the haunted mirror episode of Dead of Night.

donsiegel.description: He made tight, unsentimental thrillers about loners and institutions, mostly on modest budgets.

facts.text: Started out making montage sequences at Warner Bros., including for Casablanca.
Made five films with Clint Eastwood.

robertwiene.signature: Directed the film that defined Expressionism.
robertwiene.description: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari projects a madman's vision onto the world, with painted shadows and jagged, tilted sets.

facts.text: The sets of Caligari have light and shadow painted directly onto them.
Its story is framed as the tale of an asylum inmate.

alekseigerman.signature: Plunged the camera into crowded, chaotic recreations of Soviet history.
alekseigerman.description: He made only six features. They are dense with overlapping talk and passing figures who glance at the lens.

facts.text: Several of his films were shelved by Soviet censors for years.
Spent over a decade on Hard to Be a God, which was completed after his death.

davidhand.signature: Supervising director of Disney's first features.
davidhand.description: He coordinated the teams of sequence directors and animators on Snow White and Bambi, under Walt Disney's close control.

facts.text: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was the first American cel-animated feature.
Later set up an animation studio in Britain.

haroldramis.signature: A comedy writer-director from Chicago's Second City.
haroldramis.description: He wrote and directed some of the defining American comedies of the 1980s and 1990s.

facts.text: Groundhog Day traps its hero in the same day; fans still debate how many years pass.
Co-wrote and acted in Ghostbusters.

melbrooks.description: A television gag writer who made spoofs of the western, the horror film and the Hitchcock thriller, breaking the fourth wall at will.

facts.text: Young Frankenstein reused laboratory props from the 1931 Frankenstein.
Has won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony.
His company produced David Lynch's The Elephant Man.

derekjarman.signature: Painter, activist and the leading figure of British queer cinema.
derekjarman.description: He made low-budget films mixing Super 8 footage, tableaux and anachronism.

facts.text: Blue is a single blue screen with a soundtrack, made as he was losing his sight to an AIDS-related illness.
Was production designer on Ken Russell's The Devils.
Gave Tilda Swinton her first film roles.

guillermodeltoro.signature: Makes fairy tales in which the monsters are more humane than the people.
guillermodeltoro.description: A Mexican director who began as a make-up effects artist. His films are designed down to the last gear and creature.

facts.text: Keeps notebooks of drawings for every film.
Won Best Director and Best Picture for The Shape of Water.

jordanpeele.signature: Uses horror to expose American racism.
jordanpeele.description: He came from sketch comedy and writes his own tightly constructed, allegorical scripts.

facts.text: Was the first Black screenwriter to win the Oscar for original screenplay, for Get Out.
Was half of the comedy duo Key & Peele.

peterwatkins.signature: Stages history and future catastrophes as if television news crews were present.
peterwatkins.description: A British director who has worked mostly in exile. His films use amateur casts and interview formats to attack the conventions of mass media.

facts.text: The BBC withheld The War Game from broadcast for twenty years; it still won the documentary Oscar.
La Commune runs almost six hours, with a cast of Parisian volunteers.

oliverstone.signature: Makes aggressive, densely edited films about American power.
oliverstone.description: A Vietnam veteran who writes his own scripts. His films argue with recent American history, mixing film stocks and formats.

facts.text: Served as an infantryman in Vietnam, the basis of Platoon.
JFK mixes film formats and archive footage.
Won Best Director Oscars for Platoon and Born on the Fourth of July.

charleslaughton.signature: A great actor who directed one film, a nightmare fairy tale like nothing else in Hollywood.
charleslaughton.description: The Night of the Hunter combines silent-film lighting, storybook sets and a child's view of evil.

facts.text: The Night of the Hunter failed on release and he never directed again.
Lillian Gish, a star of D. W. Griffith's films, plays the children's protector.

barbaraloden.signature: Wrote, directed and starred in Wanda, a founding film of American independent cinema.
barbaraloden.description: An actress who made one feature, about a woman who drifts away from her life in the Pennsylvania coal country.

facts.text: Wanda was shot on 16mm with a tiny crew.
It was her only feature; she died in 1980, aged 48.
Was married to Elia Kazan.

forughfarrokhzad.signature: One of Iran's great modern poets, whose single short film seeded the Iranian New Wave.
forughfarrokhzad.description: The House Is Black sets her own verse and passages of scripture against images of daily life in a leprosy colony.

facts.text: The House Is Black was filmed in a leprosy colony.
She died in a car accident in 1967, aged 32.

fernandomeirelles.signature: Brought a kinetic, advertising-honed style to the favelas of Rio.
fernandomeirelles.description: A Brazilian director who came from television and commercials.

facts.text: City of God cast mostly non-professional young people from Rio's favelas.
Kátia Lund is credited as its co-director.

asgharfarhadi.signature: Builds moral thrillers out of domestic disputes in which everyone has their reasons.
asgharfarhadi.description: His scripts turn on a small lie or an unseen event and let class, religion and pride do the rest.

facts.text: Won the foreign-language Oscar twice, for A Separation and The Salesman.
Often withholds the decisive event, leaving the audience to judge.

saramaldoror.signature: A pioneer of African cinema, who filmed the liberation struggles of Portuguese-speaking Africa.
saramaldoror.description: Born in France to a Guadeloupean father. Her films approach the independence wars through the daily lives of women.

facts.text: Studied film in Moscow alongside Ousmane Sembène.
Was an assistant on The Battle of Algiers.
Sambizanga is set at the start of Angola's war of independence.

wangbing.signature: Documents the people left behind by China's economic transformation at monumental length.
wangbing.description: He usually works alone with a small digital camera, staying with factory workers, migrants and survivors of labour camps for months or years.

facts.text: West of the Tracks runs more than nine hours.
Usually shoots alone with a small digital camera.

medhondo.signature: A Mauritanian-born filmmaker in France who attacked colonialism with Brechtian invention.
medhondo.description: His films mix theatre, song, documentary and satire to tell the history of slavery, colonisation and immigration.

facts.text: West Indies stages centuries of the slave trade as a musical on a single ship set.
Worked for years as a voice actor dubbing films into French.

cheryldunye.signature: Blends documentary and fiction, a mix she calls the Dunyementary.
cheryldunye.description: She plays a version of herself in her films, talking to the camera about history, desire and who gets remembered.

facts.text: The Watermelon Woman is regarded as the first feature directed by a Black lesbian.
The 1930s actress it investigates is invented, complete with a fabricated photo archive.

jennielivingston.signature: Made the defining document of New York's ballroom culture.
jennielivingston.description: Paris Is Burning records the drag balls of Harlem and the houses that compete in them.

facts.text: Paris Is Burning was filmed over several years at Harlem's drag balls.
It brought voguing and ballroom slang to a wide audience.

montehellman.signature: The minimalist of the American road movie and western.
montehellman.description: He started out with Roger Corman. His films strip genre down to waiting, driving and silence.

facts.text: Two-Lane Blacktop cast the musicians James Taylor and Dennis Wilson.
It ends with the film appearing to burn in the projector.

jonathanglazer.signature: Makes about a film a decade, each a formal experiment.
jonathanglazer.description: He came from music videos and commercials. His features take a single unsettling idea and follow it with cold rigour.

facts.text: Under the Skin used hidden cameras to film real passers-by with Scarlett Johansson.
The Zone of Interest keeps the camp's atrocities off screen and on the soundtrack.

fernandoesolanas.signature: Co-author of the Third Cinema manifesto.
fernandoesolanas.description: An Argentine filmmaker and later politician. With Octavio Getino he called for a militant cinema that is neither Hollywood nor European art film.

facts.text: The Hour of the Furnaces was made and shown clandestinely in Argentina.
It was designed to be stopped for discussion during screenings.
Co-wrote Towards a Third Cinema with Octavio Getino.

hiroshiteshigahara.signature: Made existential allegories with the novelist Kōbō Abe and the composer Tōru Takemitsu.
hiroshiteshigahara.description: Their films turn skin, sand and insects into abstract textures while their heroes lose their identities.

facts.text: Woman in the Dunes earned him a Best Director Oscar nomination.
Later became head of the Sōgetsu school of ikebana founded by his father.

williamgreaves.signature: Made a film about making a film about making a film.
williamgreaves.description: A documentary producer and a pioneer of Black filmmaking on American public television.

facts.text: Symbiopsychotaxiplasm was shot in Central Park in 1968 with crews filming each other.
It was barely shown until the 1990s.
Produced the public-television series Black Journal.

sallypotter.signature: Came to film from dance and performance art.
sallypotter.description: A British director and composer whose films question gender and storytelling conventions.

facts.text: Orlando's hero lives through four centuries and changes sex, addressing the camera throughout.
Composes music for her own films.

isaotakahata.description: Miyazaki's mentor and partner. He used animation for stories of ordinary life and loss, changing visual style with each film.

facts.text: Did not draw himself; he directed animators.
His final film, The Tale of the Princess Kaguya, looks like ink and watercolour sketches.

joshuaoppenheimer.signature: Asked Indonesian death-squad veterans to re-enact their killings as movie scenes.
joshuaoppenheimer.description: The Act of Killing lets the perpetrators of the 1965 massacres stage their memories in the style of their favourite films.

facts.text: Many Indonesian crew members are credited as Anonymous for their safety.
Werner Herzog and Errol Morris signed on as executive producers.
The Look of Silence returns to the story from the victims' side.

andrzejzulawski.signature: Films emotional extremes with a camera that never stops moving and actors pushed to hysteria.
andrzejzulawski.description: A Polish director who worked largely in France after trouble with the censors at home.

facts.text: Was an assistant to Andrzej Wajda.
Isabelle Adjani won Best Actress at Cannes for Possession.
His science-fiction epic On the Silver Globe was halted by the Polish authorities.

saragomez.description: She made documentaries about race, class and machismo in revolutionary Cuba before her only feature.

facts.text: One Way or Another mixes a love story with documentary about a Havana slum clearance.
She died before it was finished; colleagues including Tomás Gutiérrez Alea completed it.

patricioguzman.signature: Has spent fifty years recording Chile's memory.
patricioguzman.description: After filming the fall of Allende he went into exile. His later films link the dictatorship's crimes to Chile's deserts, sea and mountains.

facts.text: The Battle of Chile was filmed during the run-up to the 1973 coup.
Nostalgia for the Light links astronomers and relatives searching the Atacama Desert for the disappeared.

elainemay.signature: A comic genius whose films bite harder than the studios wanted.
elainemay.description: She let scenes run long and awkward, finding comedy in cruelty and self-deception.

facts.text: Shot more than a million feet of film for Mikey and Nicky.
Was half of the comedy duo Nichols and May.
The troubled release of Ishtar ended her directing career.

miklosjancso.signature: Choreographed history as ritual on the Hungarian plain.
miklosjancso.description: Soldiers, prisoners and horsemen circle each other in endless tracking shots that turn power into abstract movement.

facts.text: Some of his films contain only a dozen or so shots.
Béla Tarr has acknowledged him as a predecessor.

masakikobayashi.signature: A pacifist who attacked authority and the samurai code.
masakikobayashi.description: His austere widescreen films show individuals crushed by military and feudal systems.

facts.text: The Human Condition trilogy runs over nine hours.
Tōru Takemitsu scored Harakiri and Kwaidan.

johnhughes.description: A former advertising copywriter who wrote and directed the defining American teen films of the 1980s.

facts.text: Wrote the script for Home Alone.
Set almost all his films in the Chicago suburbs.
Ferris Bueller talks to the audience throughout.

johnlandis.signature: Mixed anarchic comedy with other genres.
johnlandis.description: His films of the late 1970s and 1980s combine broad comedy with car chases, music and horror.

facts.text: Directed Michael Jackson's Thriller video.
An American Werewolf in London won the first Oscar for make-up.

maysles.description: The brothers filmed with lightweight equipment and no interviews or narration, trusting what unfolded in front of them.

facts.text: Gimme Shelter captured the killing at the Altamont concert on film.
The editor Charlotte Zwerin is credited as co-director of Salesman and Gimme Shelter.
Grey Gardens portrays a reclusive mother and daughter related to Jacqueline Kennedy.

blakeedwards.signature: Master of the slow-burn sight gag in wide frames.
blakeedwards.description: He staged elaborate physical comedy in long, wide takes, letting disasters build in the background.

facts.text: Created the Pink Panther series with Peter Sellers.
Worked with the composer Henry Mancini for decades.
Was married to Julie Andrews.

leniriefenstahl.signature: Put formal innovation at the service of Nazi propaganda.
leniriefenstahl.description: A dancer and actress in mountain films before Hitler commissioned her to film the Nuremberg rally. Her work remains the central case in arguments about art and politics.

facts.text: Triumph of the Will was commissioned to glorify the 1934 Nuremberg rally.
Olympia pioneered techniques of sports filming, such as tracking cameras and underwater shots.
She denied responsibility for the rest of her life.

edgargulmer.signature: Made stylish films from almost nothing on Hollywood's Poverty Row.
edgargulmer.description: A designer in Weimar Germany who spent most of his American career at the cheapest studios.

facts.text: Detour was shot in a matter of days.
Worked as a designer in Germany, including for Murnau.
Also made Yiddish-language films in the 1930s.

kiramuratova.signature: The most eccentric voice of Soviet and Ukrainian cinema.
kiramuratova.description: She worked in Odessa. Her films are abrasive and funny, full of repetition and interruption.

facts.text: Several of her films were banned or shelved until perestroika.
Her characters repeat lines over and over like broken records.

irvinkershner.signature: The character director who made the darkest Star Wars film.
irvinkershner.description: He came from documentary and television and was known for work with actors.

facts.text: Taught George Lucas at USC, who later hired him for The Empire Strikes Back.

cecilbdemille.signature: Hollywood's first showman, synonymous with the biblical epic.
cecilbdemille.description: Co-directed one of the first features shot in Hollywood and worked for five decades, mixing spectacle, piety and titillation. When Cannes commemorated its cancelled 1939 edition in 2002, a jury gave that year's prize to his Union Pacific.

facts.text: The Squaw Man (1914), which he co-directed, was among the first features made in Hollywood.
Remade his own The Ten Commandments in 1956.
Plays himself in Sunset Boulevard.

leopoldlindtberg.signature: A Vienna-born theatre director who made Swiss cinema's best-known films.
leopoldlindtberg.description: An exile from Austria who worked in Zurich. The Last Chance follows refugees crossing the Alps into Switzerland and was made while the war was still being fought.

facts.text: The Last Chance cast real Allied internees alongside actors.
Won the Golden Bear for Four in a Jeep.

emiliofernandez.signature: El Indio, who gave Mexican cinema its heroic image of land and people.
emiliofernandez.description: With the cinematographer Gabriel Figueroa he created a monumental style of low horizons, vast skies and noble faces during the golden age of Mexican cinema.

facts.text: Worked with the cinematographer Gabriel Figueroa.
Acted in Sam Peckinpah's The Wild Bunch.

frantisekcap.signature: A Czech director whose resistance drama shared the first Cannes prize.
frantisekcap.description: A prolific director of the 1940s who left Czechoslovakia after the Communist takeover and later worked in Slovenia.

facts.text: Men Without Wings deals with the reprisals that followed the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich.
Later made popular comedies in Slovenia, including Vesna.

chetananand.signature: Made the first Indian film honoured at Cannes.
chetananand.description: A founder of the Hindi film company Navketan with his brother Dev Anand. Neecha Nagar is a social allegory that drew on Soviet montage and expressionist lighting.

facts.text: Neecha Nagar is based on Gorky's The Lower Depths.
Ravi Shankar composed its music.
His brothers Dev and Vijay Anand were also major figures in Hindi cinema.

jeandelannoy.signature: A pillar of the French tradition of quality that the New Wave attacked.
jeandelannoy.description: A polished director of literary adaptations and star vehicles across five decades.

facts.text: Truffaut singled him out in his polemic against the French cinema of quality.
Directed The Eternal Return from a script by Jean Cocteau.

ipsenlauritzen.signature: The Danish duo behind the first major films about the resistance.
ipsenlauritzen.description: Ipsen was one of Denmark's great stage actresses. With Lauritzen she co-directed thrillers and war dramas in the 1940s.

facts.text: The Red Meadows is told in flashback by a resistance fighter awaiting execution.
Denmark's Bodil film awards are named after Bodil Ipsen and Bodil Kjer.

alfsjoberg.signature: Sweden's leading stage director, who won the top prize at Cannes twice.
alfsjoberg.description: Head director at Stockholm's Royal Dramatic Theatre. In Miss Julie, past and present share the same shot, an effect Bergman later developed.

facts.text: Torment was written by the young Ingmar Bergman.
In Miss Julie, figures from the past walk through the same frame as those in the present.

fridrikhermler.signature: A former secret-police agent who became a leading Soviet director.
fridrikhermler.description: Made psychologically acute silent films in Leningrad and later officially favoured dramas under Stalin.

facts.text: Fragment of an Empire follows a shell-shocked soldier who regains his memory years after the revolution.
The Turning Point shows the battle of Stalingrad from the generals' headquarters.

edwarddmytryk.signature: A noir stylist whose career was split by the blacklist.
edwarddmytryk.description: Made some of the sharpest crime films of the 1940s at RKO before the anti-Communist hearings sent him to prison and then into testimony against former colleagues.

facts.text: Was one of the Hollywood Ten, jailed for refusing to testify, and later named names.
Crossfire was one of the first Hollywood films to deal with antisemitism.

reneclement.signature: The versatile craftsman of postwar French cinema.
reneclement.description: Began in documentary and made the first great French film about the resistance, then literary adaptations and thrillers.

facts.text: The Battle of the Rails re-enacts railway sabotage with the railwaymen themselves.
Forbidden Games won the Golden Lion.
Purple Noon, with Alain Delon, was the first film about Patricia Highsmith's Tom Ripley.

bensharpsteen.signature: Supervising director of Disney's Pinocchio and Dumbo.
bensharpsteen.description: A veteran animator who coordinated Disney's features of the early 1940s and later produced the studio's nature documentaries.

facts.text: Joined Disney in 1929 as an animator.
Later produced Disney's nature documentaries.

renatocastellani.signature: A founder of pink neorealism: neorealist methods with a lighter heart.
renatocastellani.description: His comedies of young love among the poor kept the locations and amateur casts of neorealism and dropped its despair.

facts.text: Two Cents Worth of Hope cast non-professionals from a village near Naples.
Won the Golden Lion for his Romeo and Juliet in 1954.

teinosukekinugasa.signature: A former female-role actor who made Japan's boldest silent film and its first colour success abroad.
teinosukekinugasa.description: Started as an onnagata, playing women's roles, and directed for forty years. His work runs from avant-garde experiment to lavish period drama.

facts.text: A Page of Madness (1926) is an avant-garde silent set in an asylum, made without intertitles.
Gate of Hell won an honorary Academy Award and the Oscar for costume design.

delbertmann.signature: Brought the intimacy of live television drama to the cinema.
delbertmann.description: A leading director of American live television in the 1950s. Marty, about a lonely Bronx butcher, kept the small scale of its television original.

facts.text: Marty was adapted from a television play he had directed.
It is one of the few films to win both the top prize at Cannes and the Oscar for Best Picture.

jacquescousteau.signature: The oceanographer who took the film camera underwater.
jacquescousteau.description: A French naval officer and explorer whose films from the research ship Calypso showed audiences the sea floor in colour for the first time.

facts.text: Co-invented the Aqua-Lung.
The Silent World, co-directed with the young Louis Malle, also won the Oscar for documentary feature.

marcelcamus.signature: Set the Orpheus myth in the Rio carnival.
marcelcamus.description: A former assistant to several French directors. Black Orpheus, shot in Rio with a largely amateur Black cast, was a worldwide success.

facts.text: Black Orpheus helped launch bossa nova abroad through the music of Antônio Carlos Jobim and Luiz Bonfá.
It also won the foreign-language Oscar.

henricolpi.signature: An editor of the Left Bank group who directed one prize-winning film about memory.
henricolpi.description: Best known as an editor. His first feature follows a café owner who believes a passing tramp is her husband, deported during the war.

facts.text: Edited Hiroshima mon amour and Last Year at Marienbad for Alain Resnais.
The Long Absence was written by Marguerite Duras.

anselmoduarte.signature: A Brazilian star actor who directed the first South American film to win the Palme d'Or.
anselmoduarte.description: A matinee idol turned director. His success at Cannes was resented by the younger Cinema Novo directors, who saw his style as old-fashioned.

facts.text: O Pagador de Promessas follows a farmer carrying a cross to a city church to keep a vow.
It was the first South American film nominated for the foreign-language Oscar.

richardlester.signature: Gave the Swinging Sixties their film style.
richardlester.description: An American who made his career in Britain, coming from television and the Goons. His comedies are cut fast, full of visual gags and asides to the camera.

facts.text: Directed the Beatles in A Hard Day's Night and Help!
His fast cutting to music is often cited as a forerunner of the music video.

pietrogermi.signature: Moved from neorealist drama to savage comedies of Italian manners.
pietrogermi.description: His early films are social dramas set in Sicily. In the 1960s he became the sharpest satirist of Italian codes of honour and marriage.

facts.text: Divorce Italian Style won the Oscar for original screenplay.
Often acted in his own films.

claudelelouch.signature: A one-man band who shoots his own films with a roving handheld camera.
claudelelouch.description: He produces, writes and photographs romantic films built on chance meetings, music and improvisation.

facts.text: A Man and a Woman also won two Oscars.
Mixed colour and black and white in it, partly to save money.
Operates the camera himself.

eliopetri.signature: The most grotesque and furious voice of Italian political cinema.
eliopetri.description: His films turn factory work, policing and power into feverish satire, with Gian Maria Volonté in the lead.

facts.text: Investigation of a Citizen Above Suspicion won the foreign-language Oscar.
Made several films with the actor Gian Maria Volonté.
Worked often with the composer Ennio Morricone.

alanbridges.signature: A British television director with a fine ear for class.
alanbridges.description: He worked mostly in television drama. His few features are restrained period pieces about the English class system.

facts.text: The Hireling is adapted from a novel by L. P. Hartley, author of The Go-Between.
Worked mostly in television drama.

jerryschatzberg.signature: A fashion photographer who made three of the quietest films of New Hollywood.
jerryschatzberg.description: His early films observe drifters and addicts with a photographer's patience, on real streets and roads.

facts.text: Shot the cover photograph of Bob Dylan's Blonde on Blonde.
The Panic in Needle Park gave Al Pacino his first leading role.
Scarecrow was photographed by Vilmos Zsigmond.

lakhdarhamina.signature: The leading filmmaker of independent Algeria.
lakhdarhamina.description: He joined the Algerian resistance's film unit and later ran the national newsreel office. His films tell the story of colonisation and the war of independence on an epic scale.

facts.text: Chronicle of the Years of Fire was the first African and the first Arab film to win the Palme d'Or.
It traces the years leading up to the Algerian war of independence.

taviani.signature: Brothers who directed alternate scenes and merged history with fable.
taviani.description: They began as political documentarists. Their films set peasants and rebels in Italian landscapes and tell their stories with the stylisation of folk tales.

facts.text: Took turns directing, scene by scene.
Padre Padrone also won the critics' prize at Cannes.
Won the Golden Bear in 2012 for Caesar Must Die, filmed with prison inmates.

volkerschlondorff.signature: The New German Cinema's specialist in literary adaptation.
volkerschlondorff.description: He trained in France and brought its craft back to Germany, adapting Musil, Böll, Grass and Proust.

facts.text: Trained in France as an assistant to Louis Malle, Alain Resnais and Jean-Pierre Melville.
The Tin Drum also won the foreign-language Oscar.
Co-directed The Lost Honour of Katharina Blum with Margarethe von Trotta.

costagavras.description: Born in Greece and based in France. He applies the pace and suspense of the thriller to real cases of state violence.

facts.text: Z, about the assassination of a Greek politician, won the foreign-language Oscar.
Missing was his first American film.

yilmazguney.signature: A Kurdish star and director who made his greatest films from a prison cell.
yilmazguney.description: Turkey's most popular screen actor, nicknamed the Ugly King, he turned to directing films about the poor and was jailed repeatedly.

facts.text: Wrote Yol in prison; Şerif Gören shot it from his detailed instructions.
Escaped from prison in 1981 and finished the film in exile.

rolandjoffe.signature: Made two large-scale dramas of conscience in the 1980s.
rolandjoffe.description: A British theatre and television director whose first two features set individual moral choices against historical catastrophe.

facts.text: The Killing Fields was his first feature.
The Mission was scored by Ennio Morricone and photographed by Chris Menges.

billeaugust.signature: A Danish director of patient, novelistic family sagas.
billeaugust.description: Trained as a cinematographer. His best-known films are long, classical adaptations set in nineteenth- and early twentieth-century Scandinavia.

facts.text: The Best Intentions was written by Ingmar Bergman about his own parents.
Pelle the Conqueror also won the foreign-language Oscar.

stevensoderbergh.signature: Restlessly alternates between studio entertainments and experiments, usually as his own cameraman.
stevensoderbergh.description: His debut launched the American independent boom of the 1990s. Since then he has treated each film as a new formal problem.

facts.text: Won the Palme d'Or at 26 with his first feature.
Photographs and edits his own films under the names Peter Andrews and Mary Ann Bernard.
Was nominated for the Best Director Oscar twice in the same year and won for Traffic.

nannimoretti.signature: Italy's wry diarist, usually playing a version of himself.
nannimoretti.description: He writes, directs and stars in comedies about the Italian left, family and his own neuroses.

facts.text: Stars in most of his own films.
Caro diario follows him around Rome on a Vespa.
Runs his own cinema in Rome, the Nuovo Sacher.

michaelmoore.signature: Made the first-person polemic the most commercially successful kind of documentary.
michaelmoore.description: He appears in his own films as a baseball-capped everyman confronting corporations and politicians, mixing archive footage, stunts and satire.

facts.text: Fahrenheit 9/11 is the highest-grossing documentary ever released.
It was the first documentary to win the Palme d'Or since The Silent World in 1956.
Won the documentary Oscar for Bowling for Columbine.

laurentcantet.signature: Studied work, school and power through workshops with non-professional actors.
laurentcantet.description: His films grow out of long improvisation sessions with the people whose world they depict.

facts.text: The Class was developed with real pupils and stars the teacher whose book it adapts.
It was the first French film to win the Palme d'Or in 21 years.

abdellatifkechiche.signature: Films young people in very long scenes of talk and eating, shot in close-up.
abdellatifkechiche.description: Born in Tunis and raised in Nice. He shoots enormous amounts of footage to capture unguarded behaviour.

facts.text: The Cannes jury gave the 2013 Palme d'Or jointly to him and his two lead actresses.
Was born in Tunis and raised in Nice.

jacquesaudiard.signature: Brings art-film intimacy to the French crime genre.
jacquesaudiard.description: A screenwriter's son who started as a writer and editor. His films follow outsiders remaking themselves, in a tactile handheld style.

facts.text: Is the son of the screenwriter Michel Audiard.
A Prophet won the Grand Prix at Cannes.

rubenostlund.signature: Stages excruciating social embarrassment in long, fixed shots.
rubenostlund.description: A Swedish satirist of male pride and privilege who builds each film around a handful of drawn-out set pieces.

facts.text: Won the Palme d'Or for two consecutive films.
Started out making ski films.

juliaducournau.signature: Makes body horror about transformation and family.
juliaducournau.description: A French director whose films treat flesh, metal and appetite with both shock and tenderness.

facts.text: Was the second woman to win the Palme d'Or, and the first to win it alone.
Her debut feature was Raw.

justinetriet.signature: Dissects couples through talk, argument and courtroom procedure.
justinetriet.description: She began with documentaries and comedies of chaotic domestic life before turning a marriage into a trial.

facts.text: Was the third woman to win the Palme d'Or.
Anatomy of a Fall won the Oscar for original screenplay, written with Arthur Harari.

seanbaker.signature: Films people at the margins of the American economy with energy and warmth.
seanbaker.description: He casts newcomers and non-professionals, shoots on real locations and edits his own films.

facts.text: Shot Tangerine on iPhones.
Anora won five Oscars, four of them for Baker personally.
Edits his own films.
